page: Microsoft Azure L4as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Lasv4 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and includes 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The hardware configuration is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a 960 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included, and there are zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3077.78 and Geekbench single-core reaching 2079.0, both placing in the top 25%. Geekbench text processing also demonstrates strong performance at 2548.0. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6153.87 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4766.0. However, memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck; both small-block cached and large-block uncached read-only memory bandwidth fall into the bottom 25%, measuring 303.78 GB/sec and 36.89 GB/sec respectively. Database operations and Redis SET operations also show weak performance, with Redis achieving 5.97 million operations per second. Large-model LLM inference is limited, with prompt processing for a 7B model scoring in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L4as_v4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and a substantial bundled NVMe SSD, providing high resource density for memory-bound tasks without requiring larger, more expensive instance sizes. However, the weak memory read bandwidth and lower database operation benchmarks represent a tradeoff for memory-intensive transactional databases. This server is best suited for workloads such as single-threaded applications, text processing, static web serving, and lightweight memory-bound processing that can leverage the local NVMe storage while tolerating moderate memory bandwidth.
